html:
SMTO-UI-0043 — A permission rule names something SMTO doesn't have

GUID: 2e5493d2-a7cf-42b7-ad10-03aea613a72b
Slug: ui-permission-rule-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • One of your permission rules is broken, or it refers to a Skill or tool that isn't installed in SMTO any more. SMTO won't save settings that contain it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you still need the Skill the rule was for, ask the person who manages SMTO to install it again. Then select Apply in Permissions again. Once the Skill is back, the rule has something to apply to and SMTO accepts it.
  2. If you don't need it, select Permissions below the message box and write down the rules you want to keep. The rule for the missing Skill won't appear in the list. The next step clears every rule for this scope, so you'll need the list to add them back.
  3. Select Use inherited permissions (it says Reset to product default when Apply to is Global). Then add back the rules you wrote down and select Apply. Starting from the usual setup clears the broken rule along with the others for that scope.

What success looks like

  • Apply closes the Permissions window without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the name of the Skill or tool the rule was for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A permission rule has an invalid decision, unknown fields or a malformed skill_id/tool_id, or server normalization could not find its Skill or tool in the current capability registry.

What this means

  • A rule has invalid decision/fields/identifier syntax, or backend normalization cannot find its Skill or tool in the current registry. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A rule has invalid decision/fields/identifier syntax, or backend normalization cannot find its Skill or tool in the current registry.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact rule identity, allowed fields and current capability registry.

How to fix it

  • permission_policy.js canonical() throws ui_permission_rule_invalid for decisions outside allow/ask/deny, extra keys, or IDs not matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,127}$ (Skill) or skill.tool (tool); normalize_permission_policy() raises when a skill_id or tool_id is not in registry.skill_ids()/tool_ids(). Remove or correct the stale rule, or reinstall the Skill it refers to.
  • Use the supported executable, subcommand or Skill identifier and an advertised permission decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every rule names a valid advertised capability with one supported decision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
